claims.text: Applicants must be from low-income households.
Applicants must be ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
Applicants must ordinarily be resident in Scotland.
Applicants must have at least two years of secondary schooling or college in Scotland, or a substantial recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain for the course duration, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds towards tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, with exceptions for limited second-degree cases.
Applicants must have an offer or be a continuing student on an eligible undergraduate degree course.
The eligible institutions are listed Scottish universities, the Glasgow School of Art, the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, and Scotland’s Rural College (SRUC).
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026, for grants covering the academic year 2026-27.
Grants cover the cost of tuition fees up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
The purpose of the grant is to help students from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
Applications are made online.
Applicants must complete an eligibility checker before applying.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted unless the student was first informed of SAAS ineligibility after the portal closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks, provided all information and references are submitted promptly.
Supporting documents include evidence of eligibility, university course offer/enrollment, SAAS Award Notice, and income proof (P60 or payslips/Universal Credit statements).

The Carnegie Education Fund recognizes that many individuals may have encountered difficulties in gaining employment after an undergraduate degree, have suffered career setbacks, experienced health or personal issues which have forced them to reconsider their career path.
The fund has set aside a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start an undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Students who completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course are eligible for second-degree funding.
Students entering the first year of their second degree course in academic year 2026-27 are eligible.
Students who have been unable to gain employment in their previous degree subject, are unemployed, or facing redundancy are eligible for second-degree funding.
Students wishing to reskill in a different field of study unrelated to previous qualifications and recognized as a skills shortage area are eligible for second-degree funding.
Applications for second degrees are considered at the discretion of CEF.
Students who have already started a 2nd degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible to apply.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
Household income thresholds are used as guides, not hard cut-offs, and applications are reviewed holistically.
The median household income of award-holders in 2025-26 was £10,000 per year.
CEF does not accept applications for previous years of study for which the student still owes tuition fees.
The definition of 'ordinarily resident' used by CEF is the same as that used by the Student Awards Agency Scotland (SAAS).
Applicants eligible for a SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loan are expected to take full advantage of available loans.

CEF will not consider an application if the applicant is eligible for support (including loans) from Student Finance England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or any loan or grant from an overseas government or agency.
In general, CEF will not fund more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
Applications for different courses after receiving previous funding may not be considered.
Part-time students receiving tuition fee support from SAAS and not eligible for other grants, bursaries or loans may apply if the SAAS award is less than the total fees.
Students who came to Scotland solely to study at university or college without prior educational ties to Scotland are not eligible.
HNC, HND, Access courses, Accelerated degree courses with graduate entry, Open University courses, CPD courses, and university courses below degree level are not eligible.
Courses delivered by or at a university outside Scotland, or courses at a Scottish Higher Education Institute delivered and validated by a university outside Scotland, are not eligible.
Postgraduate degrees are not eligible for support.
